artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
How Big the Space" is a 2018 single by Steven Wilson, released on Caroline International as a 12-inch vinyl for Record Store Day. The track was co-written with Andy Partridge of XTC, marking a notable collaboration between two influential figures in progressive and alternative rock. Musically, the song blends Wilson's signature atmospheric rock style with subtle pop sensibilities, featuring lush arrangements, melodic hooks, and introspective lyrics. The single also includes an instrumental version, highlighting Wilson's production craftsmanship and attention to sonic detail.

Within Steven Wilson's discography, "How Big the Space" stands out as a unique, limited-edition release that bridges his solo work with his collaborative spirit. While not part of a full-length album, the single reflects Wilson's ongoing exploration of melodic songwriting and his ability to merge progressive textures with accessible pop structures. The release was well-received by fans and critics for its craftsmanship and the novelty of the Partridge collaboration, though its limited availability meant it did not achieve broad commercial success. Nonetheless, it remains a cherished entry in Wilson's catalog for its artistry and collaborative significance.
